issues.legal_issue: A Hindu family consisting of one male member, his wife, and his daughters may qualify as a Hindu Undivided Family for wealth-tax assessment.
material_facts: At the relevant time, the assessee’s family consisted of him, his wife, and two minor daughters, with no other male member.
He filed wealth-tax returns claiming assessment as a Hindu Undivided Family.
issues.conclusion: The family could be assessed as a Hindu Undivided Family even though it had only one male member.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Wealth Tax Act treats a Hindu Undivided Family, rather than only a Hindu coparcenary, as an assessable entity. The expression is understood in the sense of a Hindu joint family under Hindu personal law. A joint family includes its members’ wives and unmarried daughters and may consist of a single male member with those female family members. Kalyanji Vithaldas v. Commissioner of Income Tax supports treating the statutory expression as wider than a coparcenary.

predicates.wealth_tax_assessment: The proceeding determines the status in which property is assessed to wealth tax.
predicates.family_has_one_male_member: The family has one male member and no other male member.
predicates.family_includes_wife_or_unmarried_daught: The family includes the male member’s wife or unmarried daughters.

issues.definition: When a wealth-tax assessment concerns a family with one male member and a wife or unmarried daughters, the family qualifies as a Hindu Undivided Family assessable unit.

issues.legal_issue: Property that was joint-family property before partition retains its joint-family character when allotted to a sole coparcener who has a wife and daughters but no son.
material_facts: The assets in question had belonged to a Hindu Undivided Family before partition among the assessee, his father, and his brothers.
The assessee received his share of those assets on partition.
At the relevant time, the assessee had a wife and two minor daughters and no son or other male coparcener.
The assessee sought wealth-tax assessment of the assets as belonging to a Hindu Undivided Family, rather than to him individually.
issues.conclusion: The partition did not convert the assets into the assessee’s individual property; they remained property of the Hindu Undivided Family of the assessee, his wife, and his daughters, and the Tribunal was right to determine his status as a Hindu Undivided Family.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Wealth Tax Act makes a Hindu Undivided Family an assessable entity, and section 5(1)(ii) refers to a member’s interest in coparcenary property. The Court distinguished property that was separate property before receipt from property already impressed with the character of joint-family property. Under Hindu law, the latter does not lose that character merely because partition leaves one coparcener; the rights of existing and future family members, including a son who may be born or adopted and female members’ rights to maintenance, are relevant. Attorney General of Ceylon v. A.R. Arunachalam Chettiar and Gowali Buddanna’s case support that principle. The distinction from Kalyanji Vithaldas and the treatment of Gomedalli Lakshminarayan and A.P. Swamy Gomedalli explain why property originating as joint-family property is treated differently from separate property. T.S. Srinivasan v. Commissioner of Income Tax did not decide this issue.

rule.if: wealth_tax_assessment and property_was_joint_family_property_before_partition and coparcener_received_property_on_partition and recipient_has_wife_or_daughters and recipient_has_no_son

predicates.wealth_tax_assessment: The proceeding determines the status in which property is assessed to wealth tax.
predicates.property_was_joint_family_property_befor: The property belonged to a Hindu joint family before partition.
predicates.coparcener_received_property_on_partitio: A coparcener received the property as his share on partition.
predicates.recipient_has_wife_or_daughters: The recipient has a wife or daughters who are members of his family.
predicates.recipient_has_no_son: The recipient has no son at the relevant time.

issues.definition: When a wealth-tax assessment concerns property that was joint-family property before partition and was allotted to a coparcener with a wife or daughters but no son, the property remains family property assessable as a Hindu Undivided Family.

issues.legal_issue: A prior decision addressing when a family first arose upon conception or birth of a son does not decide whether a family consisting of a man and his wife exists, or whether partitioned joint-family property belongs to that family, before a son exists.
material_facts: The earlier case concerned a claim that a Hindu Undivided Family first came into existence when a son was conceived, rather than when he was born.

The parties in that earlier case proceeded on the basis that no Hindu Undivided Family existed before conception, and the issue of a family consisting of a man and his wife without a son was neither raised nor argued.
The present dispute concerned the status of a family that included a wife and daughters and the character of property received from a pre-existing joint family on partition.
issues.conclusion: The earlier decision had no bearing on the issue presented and did not prevent recognition of the family or its claim to the partitioned property.
issues.legal_principle: T.S. Srinivasan v. Commissioner of Income Tax decided only whether a Hindu Undivided Family claimed to arise through a conceived son came into existence upon conception or birth. Since the existence of a family consisting of a man and his wife without a son, and the character of property received on partition, were not raised or decided there, that decision does not resolve those distinct questions.

predicates.later_case_invokes_prior_family_status_d: A party in a later case relies on an earlier decision about family status.
predicates.prior_case_concerned_when_family_first_a: The earlier case addressed when a family first came into existence upon conception or birth of a son.
predicates.present_case_concerns_family_without_son: The later case concerns a family without a son or the status of property received from a joint family on partition.

issues.definition: When an earlier decision addressed only when a family first arose upon conception or birth of a son, it does not determine a later, distinct issue concerning a family without a son or property received on partition.
